name: Subliminals for appearance
lead: Subliminal audio, in the form used by looksmaxxing and self-improvement communities, consists of recordings that supposedly carry affirmations or intentions below the threshold of conscious hearing, often layered under music or sound, and are listened to in the hope of changing the body, such as growing taller, changing eye colour, improving jaw growth or reducing hair loss [1][2][3]. Listeners claim these recordings work by influencing the subconscious mind.

Wikipedia defines subliminal stimuli as sensory stimuli below an individual's threshold for conscious perception, including audio played below audible volume or masked by other sounds [4]. Laboratory research has found effects of such stimuli on brain activity and on actions a person already intends to take, but the American Psychological Association was reported in 2009 as saying there was no conclusive evidence that effects are truly subliminal [4].

No study found has tested subliminal audio for changing physical appearance. Forum threads show a mix of users reporting results, users citing placebo, and users who say the idea does not work [2][5][6][7].

paras: Appearance subliminals are audio files marketed or shared for a specific physical outcome. Thread titles show targets such as growing taller while sleeping, eye colour change, growth of both jaws and hair loss [8][9][10]. One forum poster says the community has gone from cold showers and mewing through surgeries and back to subliminals [2]. Another refers to the subreddit r/subliminals, where members make extreme claims of results .

The idea of covert persuasion became popular after cinematographer James Vicary claimed in 1957 that hidden messages in films boosted soft drink sales; Wikipedia says he later admitted inflating the results [4]. Later research found that subliminal stimuli can activate brain regions without awareness and may prime actions a person already plans to take, and a meta-analysis found no significant effect on consumer choice between two alternatives [4]. Wikipedia describes one study where thirsty participants primed with a drink brand chose it more often, but characterises it as limited [4].

Wikipedia also summarises a study of 141 undergraduates with self-concept problems randomised to rational-emotive therapy, subliminal stimulation, both or placebo. The subliminal group looked like the placebo group except for a significant improvement in self-concept and fewer related irrational cognitions [4]. The page describes the effect as limited to self-concept and does not report any physical measure.

No studies found on subliminal audio for height, facial structure, hair, eye colour or other physical appearance. General subliminal-perception research and one study of subliminal self-concept recordings exist, but they address psychological rather than physical outcomes [4].

Forum threads have titles claiming positive results [7], asking whether subliminals work [3][6], and proposing that any effect might act through placebo [5]. A results thread invited users to report outcomes [11]. Some posters say they listen to subliminals for height gain while asleep [8]. Others say they are sceptical but ask why so many users on a subreddit report extreme results .

timeline.event: James Vicary claims hidden cinema messages raised soft drink sales; he later admitted inflating the data [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org subliminals are a recurring, contested topic, with threads for and against and frequent suggestion of a placebo explanation [2][5][6][7].

claims.claim: Subliminals can change physical traits such as height, eye colour or jaw growth
claims.believers: Posters say they have had positive results or point to subreddit members reporting extreme changes, and suggest the subconscious can influence the body [7][9].
claims.experts: No published studies found have tested subliminal audio for physical change; Wikipedia says research shows subliminal stimuli mainly affect behaviours a person already intends [4].

claims.claim: Any benefit comes from placebo or expectation
claims.believers: A thread proposes subliminals may work through placebo [5].
claims.experts: In the study Wikipedia summarises, the subliminal group resembled placebo except for a self-concept improvement [4].

claims.claim: Listening to subliminals while asleep makes you grow taller
claims.believers: One poster says they listen to height subliminals during sleep [8].
claims.experts: No published studies found have examined subliminal audio and height.

card.summary: Audio tracks claimed to reshape the body via the subconscious: no study has tested physical change, and forum members themselves are split.
card.note: No published studies on physical appearance; related research concerns psychological outcomes.

quick.overview:
Appearance subliminals are audio recordings that supposedly deliver hidden messages to change features such as height, eye colour or jaw growth. They circulate on looksmaxxing forums and on subreddits dedicated to the practice.

No study has tested them for physical change. Subliminal-perception research mostly finds limited effects on behaviour a person already intends, and one self-concept trial found effects resembling placebo apart from a self-concept change.
quick.mechanism: Believers say the subconscious mind can be influenced by sub-audible affirmations. Researchers describe subliminal stimuli as stimuli below conscious perception with limited, context-dependent effects.
quick.risks: Direct physical risk is low. Wikipedia notes subliminal advertising is prohibited in several countries.
